title: fix(gateway): register TLS renewal with sidecar owner
body:
Related: #146275, #146267

## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent changes left TLS renewal using the old array-based Gateway sidecar registration call after the stop owner switched to variadic handles. The merged source fails core typechecking because the array has no `stop()` method. A TLS-enabled Gateway would register the array itself and fail to stop its renewal watcher through the lifetime owner during shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the TLS renewal handle directly to the existing sidecar stop owner. This is a one-line caller correction; TLS enablement, certificate renewal, and shutdown ownership remain unchanged.

## User Impact

TLS renewal participates in normal Gateway shutdown cleanup. No configuration, schema, stored-format, dependency, or public API change; no migration is needed.

## Evidence

- Original merged main reproduced `TS2741` in `server-startup-finish.ts`: the registered array lacks the required `stop` method.
- The corrected source passes core typechecking and targeted lint.
- Independent review through P2 found no actionable defect.
- The full build passed on `e3386ff2f238832f9b2c23e93f396c300aed57ae`.
- A real isolated TLS Gateway passed certificate/hostname-validated HTTPS and WSS over TLS 1.3. Health confirmed the config reloader was active after TLS sidecar registration. SIGTERM closed the retained WebSocket with code 1012 and exited cleanly in 103 ms with no sidecar-stop or shutdown errors. The process stopped, the port was reusable, and the synthetic private key was removed.
- Canonical package integrity/import checks passed. A fresh published 2026.9.4 updater upgraded its isolated prefix to this exact candidate in 81.6 seconds: all 12 steps, plugin convergence, existing synthetic state preservation, installed Gateway health/build RPC, four CLI lock cases, and clean shutdown passed. The standard installed-package cell used HTTP; the separate cell above provides TLS-specific proof. Package SHA-256: `1361c9a70291258a9699c71715998f31907eefc72241da766ce400e3a7bde18c`.
- Upgrade proof reused the verified task-owned npm cache. The earlier cleanup candidate's cold native-package download exceeded the unchanged canary deadline and safely refused before activation, preserving the published installation/config. No timeout or assertion was relaxed. Managed-service restart, provider inference, and the unchanged certificate-rotation matrix were not exercised.
